author: reek
body: There is no e1000 device under codex-vm -- the only NIC it emulates is an ISA NE2000 -- so nothing here touches a register, a descriptor ring or a frame. Every function in E1000e that reads or writes the device is UNTESTED and stays untested until the driver meets real hardware. This file pins the part of the driver that is decidable without the part: which PCI devices it claims, and the alignment arithmetic its rings depend on.

author: reek
body: Saying so matters more than the rows below. A green result here is evidence about device selection and nothing else, and reading it as evidence the driver works would be the exact failure this project keeps recording.

author: reek
body: The negative rows are the test. A matcher that answered True to everything would pass a positive-only suite, so each of the three ways a device can fail to be ours gets its own row: wrong vendor, wrong class, wrong subclass. The expected values are written as literals rather than computed, because a judge built out of the subject cannot fail with it.

author: reek
body: Each fixture carries its OWN device id so that find-present names which device was selected rather than merely that something was. With one id shared across the fixtures, a matcher that claimed every device would still answer find-present correctly, and the row would be decoration.

author: reek
body: e1000-poll-raw is the entry the network stack calls, and its absent guard is the only part of it reachable without a device: a zero window must answer no-frame rather than reading descriptor memory at zero.
